prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1473; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection. The insured reports the claimant's vehicle was struck on the driver's side while proceeding through a green signal. A shoulder injury is reported and the claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. No issues with the policy status were found.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which lists the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene. The report's description of the collision lines up with the damage recorded in the initial photos.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who gave the same account of the impact as the insured. Statements from two independent witnesses were also requested and are being collected.

Entry 5: Reviewed the scene photos and the vehicle damage estimate. The damage is mostly in line with a side impact of the type described, with the expected crush pattern along the driver's side.

Entry 6: Received the vehicle's prior repair history and found no earlier damage to the same areas. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start date.

Entry 7: Counsel's office provided the medical records. The reported shoulder injury fits well with the kind and force of this crash, and no earlier injury to the same body area appears in the records received.

Entry 8: Recorded a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened matches the one given at first notice and in the earlier conversation with the adjuster.

Entry 9: Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of shoulder injury. Requested updated treatment notes and a referral history to understand the timeline of care.

Entry 10: Reviewed the claimant's account against the police report, witness statements, and photos. Everything collected so far confirms the accident happened as described and that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 11: File remains open pending receipt of the updated treatment notes and counsel's demand package. Next step is to schedule a review of the medical records with the claims supervisor once those documents arrive.
